added.member: UI: CSS direction and unicode-bidi per element
added.summary: Document elements take `direction`, `unicode-bidi` and HTML's `dir` attribute (`ltr`, `rtl`, `auto`), inherited down the tree. A right-to-left element lays its flex rows, grid columns, columns and lines out from the right and aligns its start text there; logical margins, padding, borders, radii, insets, sizes and axes name the sides of each element's own direction. A declared direction sets its text's paragraph direction; `plaintext` and undeclared text keep the first strong character's, and the overrides lay text out unreordered.

fixed.member: UI: physical sides under a right-to-left surface
fixed.summary: In a right-to-left surface a document's `left`, `right`, `margin-left`, `padding-right`, `text-align: left`, `justify-content: right` and transforms stay on the side they name; before, the whole-surface mirror turned them round with the logical ones. The surface mirror still lays out documents that are right to left as a whole.
